title: Establish micro-halo illumination and token taper for dense controls
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: As we push Redwood UI into denser dashboards and compact action bars, current elevation and corner tokens produce visual noise at small scales. Buttons and table rows rely on full-surface shadows and broad radii that break rhythm in compact layouts. Charts' overlay semantics also suffer from heavyweight shadows when used in small cards.

Goal: Introduce a small-scale 'micro-halo' illumination token family and a complementary 'taper' radius/spacing axis that preserve perceived depth without dominating dense surfaces. This ticket scopes token definitions, component mapping, a migration guide, and the first pass implementation in the Buttons and Table Row components.

Proposed deliverables:
- Token spec: micro-halo-{none,1,2,3} with color/alpha, spread, blur, and directional offset tuned for 8px and 12px control heights.
- Token spec: taper-radius-{xs,sm,md} and taper-gap-{xxs,xs,sm} to create proportional corner/spacing deltas for dense modes.
- Press-depth tokens press-depth-{0..3} (subtle inset/overlay rules for interactive states).
- Usage mapping doc: how to apply tokens for Buttons, IconButtons, Selects, Table rows, DataGrid cells, and Chart small-cards.
- Migration checklist + feature flags to roll out in Console dense-mode toggle.

Success metrics (first month):
- Visual consistency score from design QA > 90% across 10 dense UI scenarios.
- No regressions in keyboard focus visibility or contrast ratio (AA) for interactive states.
- 0.1s median layout shift change measured in Console compact dashboards after rollout.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Halo tokens must remain GPU-friendly and avoid expensive backdrop filters. We will favor CSS box-shadow equivalents and tokenized RGBA values.
- Tight spacing requires careful hit-target considerations — buttons in dense mode must still meet minimum touch/keyboard targets where applicable.
- Chart overlays must degrade gracefully; heavier shadows will be converted to subtle inner glows to avoid occluding data marks.

References and artifacts:
- Figma file (design tokens board): https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/Tokens/micro-halo-proposals (comment thread: #dense-mode)
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/UX/Micro-Halo+and+Taper+Tokens+PRD
- Initial component prototypes: https://redwood.design/prototypes/dense-halo
- Related tickets: DES-314159 (token audit), DES-71234 (semantic ramp), ENG-18102 (component theming infra)
comments: 2026-03-02 - Ava Martinez: Kicked off with token research session. Collected artifacts from dashboard teams and a11y lead. Decided to prototype 3 halo intensities and 3 taper radii. Added dependency on small-hit-target audit.

2026-03-04 - Liam Chen: Implemented initial CSS variables in the token constants file (branch: feat/design/micro-halo). Early render looks promising; drop shadows are subtle at 8px heights. Filed ENG-18102 to add dense-mode theme flag at runtime.

2026-03-05 - Priya Nair (a11y): Ran contrast checks on interactive states. Halo-1 passes focus contrast when paired with 2px outline; recording guideline to retain visible focus ring in dense mode. Added label 'accessibility'.

2026-03-07 - Design review: Team feedback to reduce vertical spread of halo to avoid overlapping stacked rows. Decided to tighten blur by 12% for halo-2 and shift offsets to zero for table rows. Also decided taper-radius-xs = 4px, sm = 6px, md = 8px for initial pass.

2026-03-09 - Engineering note (Liam): Benchmarked render cost on Chrome with stale GPU; box-shadow approach OK for most pages. For very large tables we will gate halo rendering behind 'dense-shadow-heuristic' that disables halos when row-count > 1500. Added dependency ENG-19230.

2026-03-10 - Ava Martinez: Assembling migration guide. Will add step-by-step mapping for Buttons -> button-halo, TableRow -> row-halo, ChartCards -> overlay-glow. Schedule stakeholder demo for 2026-03-15.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Token JSON added to tokens-v2 with names micro-halo-0..3, taper-radius-xs..md, taper-gap-xxs..sm, press-depth-0..3. 2) Buttons and TableRow components accept denseMode prop and render new tokens behind a feature flag. 3) Design QA checklist signed off. 4) Automated visual diffs show only intended dense-mode changes in 10 scenarios.
qa_checklist:
- Visual QA on Chrome/Firefox/Safari at 100% and 125% zoom
- Keyboard focus tests preserved
- Contrast checks for interactive states >= AA
- Performance: no >5% regression in paint time for compact dashboards
- Regression screenshots for primary flows
notes: Follow-up tickets will expand token taper axis to charts and create a migration script to backfill legacy tokens to new taper aliases. Consider adding a CLI lint rule to forbid direct hard-coded shadows in components in favor of token variables.
